brief: TS Lombard maps political risk from the US midterms to markets. Base case, in line with consensus and prediction markets (>60% odds of a sweep, ~90% House), is Democrats take at least one and likely both chambers in November; Trump's approval is net underwater even on immigration, his best issue, and Democrats now lead on the economy for the first time since 2010, while high gas and diesel prices put red farm states in play. The bigger the blue wave, the less post-election disruption should weigh on sentiment; a fizzled wave raises disruption risk and volatility, though the AI trade could still benefit. Three asymmetric waves follow Election Day: Wave 1 (1-8 Nov) risks Insurrection Act invocation, the highest-volatility scenario; Wave 2 (certification, through mid-Dec) risks federal seizure of ballots or voting machines; Wave 3 (new Congress convening Jan 3) risks a Clerk-seating standoff and constitutional crisis. Six in 10 Americans doubt Trump would accept a Democratic win. Other risks: possible Iran escalation (the bank expects de-escalation after, capping oil below triple digits), delayed Trump-Xi meetings threatening the US-China trade détente, and a government shutdown by 11 Dec. Recommended hedge: tactical long gold and long VIX futures, with spot VIX low and term structure flat.
